behavior: A merged handler stops the handlers to its left only when a handler to its right calls `event.preventVaseUIHandler()` during the same call. A call in a listener of a child element does not stop the handlers of a parent element, and a call in a capture listener does not stop the bubble handlers. A tooltip around another part thus opens on focus and closes on a press when a listener of the inner part calls the method. An earlier handler that a props function calls itself runs with the rules of its own merge. `event.vaseUIHandlerPrevented` stays `true` for the rest of the dispatch. `Combobox.Chips` and `Combobox.InputGroup` read it, and they do not handle a press that a listener of a child part stopped. `Select.Popup` reads it, and it does not move the highlight for a key that a listener of a child part stopped. In Base UI, each merged handler reads the flag on the React event of the phase. A call in a child element then stops each handler of a parent element that has a handler to its right, and a lone handler of the parent still runs. A merged handler that a props function calls after the call runs only its rightmost handler.
